notes: Frozen item bank v1.0 for the twin evaluation (docs/PLAN_UNIFIED.md section 3.5, docs/research/D4). ipip50: Goldberg's 50 Big-Five Factor Markers verbatim from ipip.ori.org (public domain); ids IPIP_<domain><n> follow the key page order within each factor (+ keyed items first, then - keyed); domains E, A, C, N, O where N = Factor IV Emotional Stability (a HIGH scale score = more stable) and O = Factor V Intellect/Imagination; likert5 answers are 1-5 on the IPIP anchors, reverse = (key == '-'). game: five economic games with D4's fixed parameters, wording written for this project. gold: the profile's 20 frozen Eval questions (items.py overrides text by Q-id from the current profile; an item with an 'excluded' key is skipped and reported, GOLD_Q-12 = politics). gss: 37 non-political GSS Replicating Core items; wording and value labels verified from NORC's GSS 2022 Codebook PDF (and the cumulative codebook where the 2022 label is clipped); interviewer instructions in parentheses were dropped; options are the NORC value labels verbatim except three codebook misspellings corrected to the question wording (noted per item). Political blacklist and every excluded candidate are in docs/items_licensing.md. Do not edit items in place after this date; bump version instead.

items.text: Dictator game. You have been given 10 tokens. You may give any whole number of tokens, from 0 to 10, to an anonymous stranger who has nothing; you keep the rest. The stranger cannot respond. How many tokens do you give?
items.source_note: Forsythe, Horowitz, Savin & Sefton (1994), Games and Economic Behavior 6(3). Standard parametrization (endowment 10, give 0-10); wording is this project's own.

items.text: Trust game, as the sender. You have 10 tokens. You may send any whole number of tokens, from 0 to 10, to an anonymous stranger. Whatever you send is tripled before it reaches them; they then decide how much of the tripled amount, if any, to return to you. How many tokens do you send?
items.source_note: Berg, Dickhaut & McCabe (1995), Games and Economic Behavior 10(1). Endowment 10, sent amount tripled; wording is this project's own.

items.text: Trust game, as the receiver. An anonymous stranger sent you tokens; the amount was tripled on the way, so you now hold the tripled amount. You decide what fraction of it to send back to them, from 0 (keep everything) to 1 (return everything). What fraction do you return?
items.source_note: Berg, Dickhaut & McCabe (1995) trustee decision, expressed as a fraction 0-1 of the tripled amount; wording is this project's own.

items.text: Public goods game. You are in a group of 4 people; each of you has 10 tokens. Each person chooses how many tokens, from 0 to 10, to put into a shared pot and keeps the rest. The pot is multiplied by 1.6 and split equally among all 4 members no matter what each contributed. How many tokens do you contribute?
items.source_note: Standard linear public goods game with D4's parameters (group of 4, endowment 10, multiplier 1.6, i.e. marginal per-capita return 0.4); wording is this project's own.

items.text: Prisoner's dilemma, one shot. You and an anonymous stranger each choose, at the same time and without talking, to cooperate or defect. If you both cooperate you each get 3 tokens. If you both defect you each get 1 token. If you defect while the other cooperates you get 5 tokens and they get 0; if you cooperate while the other defects you get 0 and they get 5. Do you cooperate or defect?
items.source_note: Standard one-shot prisoner's dilemma with D4's payoff matrix (T=5, R=3, P=1, S=0) stated in the text; wording is this project's own.

items.text: Which of the statements comes closest to expressing what you believe about God? I don't believe in God (DON'T BELIEVE). I don't know whether there is a God and I don't believe there is any way to find out (DON'T KNOW, NO WAY TO FIND OUT). I don't believe in a personal God, but I do believe in a Higher Power of some kind (HIGHER POWER). I find myself believing in God some of the time, but not at others (BELIEVE SOMETIMES). While I have doubts, I feel that I do believe in God (BELIEVE WITH DOUBTS). I know God really exists and I have no doubts about it (NO DOUBTS).
options: DON'T KNOW, NO WAY TO FIND OUT
items.source_note: GSS 2022 Codebook (Release 4, November 21, 2024), 'Replicating Core', codebook page 300; value labels verbatim. The six full statements are verified from NORC's cumulative codebook main body, item 391 (https://gss.norc.org/content/dam/gss/get-documentation/pdf/codebook/GSS_Codebook_mainbody.pdf); the option labels are the 2022 codebook value labels.

items.text: Which of these statements comes closest to describing your feelings about the Bible? A. The Bible is the actual word of God and is to be taken literally, word for word (WORD OF GOD). B. The Bible is the inspired word of God but not everything in it should be taken literally, word for word (INSPIRED WORD). C. The Bible is an ancient book of fables, legends, history, and moral precepts recorded by man (ANCIENT BOOK).
items.source_note: GSS 2022 Codebook (Release 4, November 21, 2024), 'Replicating Core', codebook page 231; value labels verbatim. The 2022 codebook clips statement B and omits C; the three statements are verified from NORC's cumulative codebook main body, item 137 A (https://gss.norc.org/content/dam/gss/get-documentation/pdf/codebook/GSS_Codebook_mainbody.pdf). 'OTHER' is the codebook's volunteered-response label (code 4).
